articleTitle: A 15 W, 14-14.5 GHz solid state power amplifier
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: With the recent advancement of GaAs MESFET device technology, the power output capability of MESFETs has been increasing steadily. The solid state power amplifiers developed up to the present in C-band to Ku-band frequencies have superior performances and can replace TWT amplifiers in a communication system. SSPA Microwave Corporation 15 watt, 14-14.5 GHz solid state power amplifier which has been developed and manufactured successfully is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A K-band (30 GHz) image rejection mixer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: Describes K-band image rejection mixer/preamplifiers constructed using waveguide integrated package (WIP) techniques. Noise figures of 10 dB and conversion gains of 20 dB have been achieved over 10% bandwidth at K-band. A mixer centred at 29 GHz for communication applications is fully detailed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 0.5 to 3 GHz monolithic microwave amplifier
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: A monolithic gallium arsenide amplifier is required for use in the IF stage of a millimetre-wave downconverter. These downconverters will be used in a demonstration of TV distribution at 29 GHz. GaAs MMICs are important in providing the low cost technology demanded by this type of application. The specifications for the IF stage of this downconverter are a frequency range of 0.95 to 1.75 GHz; gain of >40 dB; noise figure of <3 dB; and VSWR of <2:1. In order to meet the gain requirement, two amplifiers will be used in series. It was decided to use a commercial foundry to fabricate the design because of the availability of accurate circuit models. These are derived from the statistical analysis of measurement data on standard components such as FETs, spiral inductors and MIM capacitors. This factor should result in a relatively short design period and a high probability of the first design iteration working. In addition the use of a well established process should result in a high yield. The foundry chosen was Tri-Quint Semiconductor, Beaverton, Oregon, USA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software generation of microwave transistor amplifier circuits
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: A new technique for the computer growth and optimisation of electrical networks is being used to design microwave amplifiers. Transistors are represented by their experimental A-parameters. Simple amplifiers, produced from the simplest of starting circuits, have a very good theoretical performance over a wide bandwidth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A highly temperature stabilized K-band (18-26.5 GHz) Gunn VCO for high capacity digital radio systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: Gunn oscillators have been designed for use in a quaternary phase shift key (QPSK) high capacity digital data link radio system, operating over the 17.7 to 19.7 GHz region, which exhibit a high degree of frequency stability with no detectable phase hit characteristics over a wide temperature range (-20 degrees C to +70 degrees C). The basic design incorporates a single Gunn diode, an electronic tuning varactor used with AFC to control the frequency and a second frequency modulation varactor. This latter varactor provides a service band facility and engineers order wire (EOW) information which is frequency modulated with low frequency signals on the transmit oscillators. A continuous mechanical tuning capability required for channel selection over a nominal 770 MHz bandwidth, is also included in this design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 60 GHz integrated E-plane RF subsystem for low cost communications applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: There is a potentially large market for wideband millimetre wave radio systems for applications such as local area communications, multichannel TV distribution, microcellular networks, industrial and intra-office communications and cordless data links. Whilst millimetre-wave monolithic (M/sup 3/IC) technology may ultimately fulfil the RF hardware requirement, this paper describes an integrated V-band (50-75 GHz) RF subsystem realised in E-plane technology which can be used to demonstrate the above applications whilst offering a potentially low cost solution. The unit employs a split housing construction to accommodate E-plane components allowing the required waveguide channels to be machined in a mass producible manner. In the same housing is a novel E-plane compatible Gunn diode oscillator. This integrated unit was then evaluated in an intra office environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: Describes the development of a low noise GaAs MESFET amplifier for use in the 30 GHz satellite communication band. The aspects covered include the choice of a suitable substrate material and the development of the MESFET through various design aspects to single stage gain module results and overall amplifier performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the bilinear transformation to broad-band microwave amplifier design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: A microwave amplifier will give maximum gain when it is fed from a signal source which presents an impedance to the amplifier which is, in general, different from the characteristic impedance of the feeder. A similar situation arises at the output. Further, if noise figure is to be minimized, input and output impedances are required which again are not the characteristic impedances of the input or output lines nor are they the same impedances required to maximize the gain. It is well known that reflection coefficients along a lossless transmission line system are related by bilinear transformations. In such transformations, circles transform into other circles or (exceptionally) into straight lines. Therefore it is to be expected that the unknown loci will be another family of circles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low cost synthesised sources for VSAT frequency converter applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: Discusses the production of low-cost downconverters for very small aperture (VSAT) receivers. It is tempting to use a proprietary low-noise block downconverter (LNB) used for the SHF to UHF conversion stage. The LNB employs a dielectric resonator oscillator (DRO) as the SHF local oscillator (LO). As an alternative the DRO can be substituted by an externally synthesised LO using a digital divider and phase detector. A wide tuning range VCO is used as a UHF reference oscillator which employs a low Q resonator, such that its phase noise is reduced by phase locking to a UHF reference. Close to carrier phase noise then becomes dominated by the crystal resonator of the UHF reference. In the critical region around the edge of the carrier recovery loop bandwidth, the phase detector/divider chain phase jitter is also important. A diagram of the phase-frequency detector is shown and was chosen because of its self acquisition properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linear varactor upconverters for use in digital microwave radio
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Components in Telecommunications
abstract: Frequency upconverters used on modern digital radios, must achieve a high degree of linearity. The theory and design of such an upconverter using a varactor diode is explained. A comparison is made between theoretical design and practical results for an upconverter operating in the range 3.8 to 4.2 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
